data.title: Spain demands justice after killing of student in Mexico
data.description:
Spain's foreign minister on Monday demanded justice after the killing of a 21-year-old Spanish student in central Mexico, a case local authorities are investigating as a femicide.

"We want to get to the bottom of this," Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares told reporters, adding authorities were in contact with the family of the woman, identified as Claudia Tacoronte.

Tacoronte, a student at the University of Granada, was in Mexico on an academic exchange program with the Autonomous University of the State of Morelos. Her body was found late on Saturday near the Casa de Cultura in Cuautla, a city in Morelos state, about 100 km (62 miles) south of Mexico City.

Local Mexican media, citing police sources, reported that she died of stab wounds. She had been in Morelos for less than a month, state prosecutor Fernando Blumenkron told journalists, and had been staying at the cultural center for a medicinal plant festival.

Spain's Equality Minister Ana Redondo said on social media that Tacoronte's exchange should have been "an experience of learning and freedom," adding that sexist violence "knows no borders and no age."

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said federal authorities were supporting the investigation.

Students at the Mexican university held a silent vigil on Monday and called on authorities to deliver justice. Some also urged stronger protections for female students, citing other recent killings of women in the state.

The University of Granada condemned the killing and held a minute of silence in Tacoronte's memory. According to Spanish newspaper El Pais, the university has also canceled exchange placements for three students who had been due to study in Morelos next semester.

Mexico has long struggled with high levels of gender-based violence. Morelos recorded 21 femicides between January and July this year, according to official data, while 380 were registered nationwide over the same period.

data.title: Toppoint Holdings Plans Reincorporation to Delaware From Nevada
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Toppoint Holdings said it plans to reincorporate in Delaware, returning from Nevada, which has been its home state since 2022.

The reincorporation is expected to become effective on or about Sept. 25, the company said.

In connection with the reincorporation, the number of shares of common stock the company is authorized to issue is expected to increase to 1 billion shares from 300 million shares. The increase won't, by itself, result in the issuance of any additional shares, Toppoint said.

Toppoint is a truckload services and solutions provider focused on the recycling export supply chain, it said.

data.title: US NTSB says one-third of FAA answers to safety recommendations are 'unacceptable'
data.description:
By David Shepardson

The U.S. National Transportation Safety Board said responses by the Federal Aviation Administration to 11 of 33 recommendations made by the board after a 2025 mid-air collision killed 67 people near Washington were "unacceptable" and failed to address safety concerns.

The January 2025 collision of an American Airlines regional jet and an Army Black Hawk helicopter near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport was the deadliest U.S. aviation disaster in more than two decades.

The NTSB said the FAA had not agreed to mandate a key safety system known as ADS-B In, which was one of the board's recommendations.

NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said the system could have given the passenger plane pilot an alert 59 seconds before the collision and the helicopter crew 48 seconds before the collision.

"How many more decades have to go by before we again and again and again have to recommend it after terrible tragedy?" Homendy told Reuters.

Homendy and families from some of those killed in the collision will again urge Congress on Tuesday to pass legislation to address the causes of the accident.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told Reuters in July ⁠the FAA could move forward on ADS-B without action from Congress but would prefer direction from lawmakers.

In a letter seen by Reuters detailing its responses to the safety board on Tuesday, the FAA said it is reviewing helicopter routes in six major cities, has completed reviews of routes in four cities, and has issued a directive to keep planes and helicopters separate.

The NTSB said Monday the FAA did not indicate if it intends to write rules to require ADS-B In.

The safety board makes recommendations and then issues status updates on its push to convince regulators to make changes. It labels them unacceptable if the agency disagrees with the recommendation, offers an alternative the NTSB finds would not address the concern, or fails to take action in a timely fashion.

In January, the NTSB found systemic failures by ​the FAA led to the 2025 collision, the worst U.S. aviation disaster since 2001. It said the accident was caused by the FAA’s decision to allow ⁠helicopters ​to travel close to the airport with no safeguards ​to separate them from airplanes and its failure to review data and act on recommendations to move helicopter ​traffic away from the airport.

The U.S. ​House of Representatives in April voted 396-10 to pass a sweeping aviation safety ​reform bill to address dozens of recommendations, while a rival bill known as the ROTOR Act passed the U.S. ​Senate unanimously in December but needed a two-thirds majority in the House to pass under fast-track rules and it fell one vote short.

data.title: CenterPoint Energy discloses customer data breach in SEC filing
data.description:
CenterPoint Energy said on Monday in an SEC filing it became aware in September of an online post claiming to have obtained a data set of certain customer information.

  • The Texas-based utility said it activated its cybersecurity incident response protocols and enlisted third-party cybersecurity experts after learning of the post, while also taking steps to further protect its systems.

  • The company said its investigation determined that an unauthorized third party obtained personal information relating to a portion of its customers through one of its external-facing systems.

  • CenterPoint said its electric and gas services have not been affected and remain operational, and it does not currently believe the incident is reasonably likely to have a material impact on its financial condition or results of operations.

  • The utility added that it has incurred, and expects to continue incurring, expenses tied to the incident and its response, but said it carries cybersecurity insurance that it believes will offset related costs.

  • CenterPoint did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

data.title: Crown Castle CFO to Retire, COO to Exit
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Crown Castle is losing its chief financial and operating officers.

The company said Monday that Chief Financial Officer Sunit Patel will retire March 31. He will be succeeded by Chief Commercial Officer Kris Hinson, effective April 1.

Chief Operating Officer Cathy Piche is also leaving the company, effective Sept. 23, to pursue other endeavors, the company said. She will continue to serve as an adviser to support the transition through Feb. 22.

Crown Castle said it has launched a search for her replacement.

data.title: QBit Semiconductor Targets Physical AI and Drone Markets with QB88XX Series Integrating Robot "Cerebellum" Control
data.description:
TAIPEI, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- QBit Semiconductor (TWO: 7913), a Taiwan-based fabless IC design leader in high-end image processing and motion control, unveiled its robotics and drone chipset roadmap at SEMICON Taiwan 2026, targeting Physical AI control opportunities.

To address space and power constraints in Dexterous Robotic Hands with over 20 degrees of freedom, QBit introduced the highly integrated QB88XX series. The SoC consolidates multi-joint control onto a single chip, reducing system costs and energy consumption. Built on a Cerebellar Model Articulation Controller (CMAC) architecture, it combines quad-core Arm Cortex-A78 processors and an NPU to execute brain commands, in addition, the Arm Cortex-M7, TGEN, and secondary NPU for motor servo control. Supporting up to 32 motors and AI servo tuning, it integrates PCIe, USB, CAN Bus, and camera interfaces for robotic arms and industrial automation.

For Drones, QBit is executing a two-phase strategy:

  • Phase 1 (2026–2028): Penetrating entry-level markets with the QB77XX, supporting up to 32GB LPDDR5/5X, PCIe, USB 3.2, and GbE. Powered by TGEN and Cortex-M33 for real-time flight control, it reduces board counts across mission computers and flight controllers.
  • Phase 2 (2029 Onward): Launching a drone-dedicated QB88XX SoC unifying flight control and mission computing into a single chip with optical flow control and target tracking.

QBit also demonstrated its QB77XX single-object tracking solution, maintaining locks during visual occlusions (tested at relative speeds up to 60 km/h with 10–15 minute flight times). Multi-object tracking will be showcased in Q4 2026.

For cybersecurity, QBit's QB7 series passed U.S. NIST CAVP validation for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) ML-DSA algorithms in 2025. The drone solutions incorporate PQC-secured boot for device authentication and firmware defense.

About QBit Semiconductor:

Headquartered in Taiwan, QBit Semiconductor (TWO: 7913) is a fabless IC design company specializing in high-end image processing, precision motion control, Edge AI, and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) SoCs, delivering one-stop ASIC design and system integration for robotics, drones, and secure terminals.

Media Contact: media@qbitsemi.com

SOURCE QBit Semiconductor LTD.
